figureObjective: Draw a to-scale principal-ray mechanism for a convex lens with f = 0.50 m and do = 0.75 m, producing a real inverted image at di = 1.5 m with m = -2.0.

claims.text: A ray entering the converging lens parallel to the optical axis exits through the far focal point.
A ray through the center of the lens continues without changing direction.
A ray entering through the near focal point exits parallel to the optical axis.
The refracted rays cross at a projectable real image.
For f = +0.50 m and do = +0.75 m, the thin-lens relation gives di = +1.5 m and magnification m = -2.0, so the image is real, inverted, and twice the object height.

elements.meaning: Reference axis through the lens center and both focal points.
Thin converging lens with focal length f = +0.50 m.
Upright object at do = +0.75 m on the incident-light side.
Focal point on the image side through which the parallel incident ray refracts.
Focal point on the object side through which the third incident ray travels.
Inverted image at di = +1.5 m with magnification -2.0.

allowedVariation.rule: The diagram may be uniformly scaled if the relative distances 0.50 m, 0.75 m, and 1.5 m remain geometrically consistent.
Ray colors and line styles may vary if the three ray paths and all arrow directions remain distinguishable.

mutations.description: Route the parallel incident ray away from the far focal point or bend the center ray.
Label the result upright or virtual despite do = 0.75 m and f = 0.50 m.
Remove ray arrowheads, swap focal labels, or place the image at 0.15 m while retaining the 1.5 m label.
